nodes.name: Ni foam surface sulfuration
nodes.procedure: Converting the surface of commercial Ni foam to NiSx by a solvothermal reaction of Ni foam with elemental sulfur in toluene (SI Appendix, Materials and Methods).
nodes.source_text: first converting the surface of Ni foam to NiSx by devising a solvothermal reaction of Ni foam with elemental sulfur in toluene (SI Appendix, Materials and Methods)

nodes.name: NiFe electrodeposition on NiSx
nodes.procedure: After formation of the NiSx layer on Ni foam, an OER-active NiFe hydroxide was electrodeposited via the reduction of nitrate from a solution of Ni(NO3)2 and Fe(NO3)3 (Ni:Fe = 3:1) (Fig. 1A) (20, 25).
nodes.source_text: After formation of the NiSx layer, an OER-active NiFe hydroxide (20-24) was electrodeposited via the reduction of nitrate from a solution of Ni(NO3)2 and Fe(NO3)3 (Ni:Fe = 3:1)

nodes.description: OER CV/LSV after activation in alkaline simulated seawater
nodes.source_text: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) showed a 30 mV lower onset overpotential... A high current density of 400 mA/cm² at an overpotential of η = 510 mV was reached (no iR compensation, R = 0.7±0.05 ohm). After iR compensation, the actual overpotential applied on the Ni³ anode to achieve an OER current density of 400 mA/cm² was ∼0.3 V

nodes.description: Two-electrode seawater splitting (Ni³ anode + Ni-NiO-Cr₂O₃ cathode) at 400 mA/cm² room temp

electrolyte.value: 1 M KOH + real seawater (San Francisco Bay)

nodes.source_text: The electrolyzer operated at a current density of 400 mA/cm² under a voltage of 2.12 V (Fig. 2C, without iR compensation; R = 0.95±0.05 ohm) continuously for more than 1,000 h without obvious decay

nodes.description: Two-electrode seawater splitting in high salinity at 400 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: voltages of the electrolyzers using the activated Ni³ anode afforded a current density of 400 mA/cm² at lower cell voltages of 2.09 V and 2.02 V, respectively. The electrolysis was still stable for more than 1,000 h
needing only 1.72 V to reach a current density of 400 mA/cm² in 6 M KOH + 1.5 M NaCl at 80°C for >1,000 h

nodes.description: High current density OER three-electrode test
nodes.source_text: Three-electrode testing of an activated Ni³ electrode in simulated alkaline seawater electrolyte showed a 750 mV overpotential (without iR compensation) for reaching a high OER current density of 1,500 mA·cm⁻²

Three-electrode linear scan voltammetry of the Ni-NiO Cr₂O₃ showed that ∼0.37 V overpotential was required to drive an HER current density of 500 mA/cm² (SI Appendix, Fig. S3A, without iR compensation). After iR compensation, the overpotential applied on the catalyst to drive a current density of 500 mA/cm² was as low as ∼160 mV

nodes.description: High current density two-electrode electrolysis at multiple currents
nodes.source_text: Two-electrode electrolysis in 1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl showed a cell voltage of 2.06 V, 2.27 V, and 2.44 V for a current density of 400, 800, and 1,000 mA/cm², respectively, all without obvious performance decay for more than 500 h at such high currents. The R_FE tests running at 400, 800, and 1,000 mA/cm² all showed nearly 100% for oxygen generation

nodes.description: Solar-driven seawater electrolysis with perovskite tandem cells
nodes.source_text: The light-driven electrolysis rate corresponded to a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 11.9±0.1% comparable to similar systems that utilize purified water. The integrated solar-driven seawater-splitting system operated stably for 20 h without obvious STH decay

nodes.description: Commercial Si solar cell-driven seawater electrolysis
nodes.source_text: A photo showing a commercial silicon solar cell-driven electrolysis (1 cm² electrodes) of seawater running at 876 mA under a voltage of 2.75 V (R = 1.0±0.05 ohms)

After 3 to 4 h of anodization in 1 M KOH plus 0.5 M NaCl at 400 mA/cm², an obvious voltage dip... After the voltage dip and over 12-h continued activation, the voltage stabilized and the oxygen R_FE increased to a stable ∼100%

nodes.characterization_summary: Electron diffraction patterns reveal that the NiSx and NiFe layers were amorphous in nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron diffraction patterns revealed that the NiSx and NiFe layers were amorphous in nature (SI Appendix, Fig. S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show ~1- to 2 μm-thick NiSx layer formed on Ni foam with ~200-nm-thick NiFe layer on top.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM (Fig. 1 B and C) and cross-sectional elemental mapping revealed a ~1- to 2μm-thick NiSx layer formed on Ni foam (SI Appendix, Fig. S2), with a ~200-nm-thick NiFe layer on top of the NiSx layer (Fig. 1 D and E).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-sectional elemental mapping reveals Ni wire, NiSx, and NiFe layers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM (Fig. 1 B and C) and cross-sectional elemental mapping revealed a ~1- to 2μm-thick NiSx layer formed on Ni foam (SI Appendix, Fig. S2), with a ~200-nm-thick NiFe layer on top of the NiSx layer (Fig. 1 D and E).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectroscopy shows vibrational modes at 470 cm⁻¹ and 540 cm⁻¹ characteristic of NiFe LDHs, peaks around 1,230 cm⁻¹, 1,440 cm⁻¹, and 1,590 cm⁻¹ assigned to S-O vibration, and strong sulfate vibrational modes at ~930 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy of the Ni³ electrode after anodic activation revealed vibrational modes at 470 cm⁻¹ and 540 cm⁻¹ characteristic of NiFe LDHs (Fig. 4C) (30), with the peaks around 1,230 cm⁻¹, 1,440 cm⁻¹, and 1,590 cm⁻¹ assigned to S-O vibration (31).

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS mapping reveals presence of both sulfate (SO₄⁻/SO₄²⁻/SO₃⁻/SO₃²⁻ from m/z = 96/48/80/40) and carbonate (CO₃⁻/CO₃²⁻ from m/z = 60/30) species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TOF secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) mapping on a Ni³ electrode after activation unambiguously revealed the presence of both sulfate and carbonate species (Fig. 4D).

nodes.characterization_summary: 3D X-ray microtomography shows structural integrity of Ni³ anode after 1,000 h seawater electrolysis similar to before electrolysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrode structures (before and after seawater splitting in various electrolytes) were investigated by 3D X-ray microtomography (SI Appendix, Fig. S8).
